title: CRDTs
summary: Conflict-free Replicated Data Types merge concurrent updates without coordination. They enable local-first and multi-master designs when you can accept their semantics and metadata costs.

sections.title: Why CRDTs
paragraphs: When replicas accept writes offline, conflicts happen. CRDTs mathematically guarantee convergence with defined merge functions — G-Counter, OR-Set, LWW-Register, and richer text types.

sections.title: State vs operation based
paragraphs: State-based (CvRDT) gossip full state merges; op-based (CmRDT) reliably deliver operations. Trade bandwidth vs delivery assumptions.

sections.title: Costs and limits
paragraphs: Metadata growth (tombstones, version vectors) needs compaction. Not every business invariant is mergeable — money transfer is the classic counterexample without extra constraints.

sections.title: Fit
paragraphs: Collaborative editing, presence, feature flags, shopping carts — good fits. Banking ledgers — usually not without additional protocol.

deepDive.title: CRDTs — Operations
paragraphs: Operating CRDTs in production means defining SLIs before tuning knobs, knowing amplification costs, and rehearsing failure modes.
Prefer reversible changes, feature flags, and canaries. Measure p50/p99 and error rate under load that matches production skew.
bullets: Define capacity from the scarcest resource
Keep rollback cheaper than forward repair when possible

deepDive.title: CRDTs — Failure modes
paragraphs: Common failures around CRDTs include overload, partial dependency outages, and silent correctness bugs that pass happy-path tests.
Inject faults in staging: latency, loss, clock skew, and disk full. Verify alerts fire and degradation is intentional.

expert.title: CRDTs — Expert notes
paragraphs: At the expert level, CRDTs intersects multi-region consistency, cost envelopes, and organizational constraints (team ownership, on-call load).
Write down the non-goals. Many outages come from optimizing a metric that was never the product requirement.

whyItMatters: Offline-first and multi-region active-active designs need conflict strategies — CRDTs are a primary tool.
reflectionQuestions: Which of your data types are naturally mergeable?
numbersToKnow: Know your p99 latency budget before adding hops
Peak load ≠ average load — plan headroom (often 2–3×)
Cross-region RTT is often ~50–150ms one way
